defects.where: badge-01..10 name block (e.g. badge-01, badge-04 views)
defects.what: Name-block rhythm is uneven: big gap (~90 px) between first and last name and a smaller one to the company, so the names read as two separate blocks rather than one
The long last name sits tight to the company line, much tighter than the same gap on the other badges, so the vertical rhythm differs from badge to badge
Company line removed cleanly but the block is not re-centred, so there is a dead band above the bar
Badges butt together with no gutter or bleed: a slight trim error leaves slivers of the next badge's bar
The last two rows sit at the top of the 3-row grid, so they are not centred on the page

EMLW.craft_notes: Clean centred Inter layout with an embedded vector PDF, tracked role labels and correct contrast (white on navy). CJK is set in a matching bold weight. It is generic: the role colour appears only on the bar, the header rule is pale grey, and the name block spacing is loose and uneven.
EMLW.revision_notes: badge-11 (Iris Van der Berg, Lowtide Labs, Speaker amber) added. The Sponsor bar is now #6b3f69 with white label on badges 05 and 09; per-pixel diff shows only the bar region changed. PDF page 2 adds the 11th badge in slot 5 with crop marks. No drift elsewhere.

defects.where: badge-05 view / page-1 crop-2-1 (花子 山田)
defects.what: CJK name falls back to a regular-weight face (WenQuanYi) while every Latin name is bold, so this badge looks lighter and off-system
PNGs carry no 300 dpi metadata (pixel size is correct)
Badges abut with no gutter or bleed; the cream ground and bars meet the neighbouring badge directly at the cut
The last two rows sit at the top of the 3-row grid, so they are not centred on the page

KCBV.craft_notes: Strongest system: a left-aligned grid, warm cream ground, a header rule in the role colour that ties top to bar, and widely tracked role labels. The scale steps clearly from first name to last name to company, and long names are scaled to fit within the margins. Embedded Instrument Sans in a vector PDF. The only real blemish is the light-weight CJK fallback.
KCBV.revision_notes: badge-11 added correctly with an amber bar and matching amber rule. Sponsor badges 05 and 09 switched to plum for both the bar and the header rule (the rule is part of the role colour system, so this is expected), with a white label for contrast. Diffs confine changes to those badges and the affected PDF slots. Iris appears on page 2 in slot 5.

defects.where: badge-01..10 name block (e.g. badge-01, badge-04, badge-10 views)
defects.what: Leading between first and last name is very tight (Bartholomew / Featherstonehaugh nearly touch; Quinn and Mensah-Bonsu jammed under the first name), while the company gap varies badge to badge
Role label set in very heavy, untracked DejaVu Sans Bold at near-bar height, so it feels crude and competes with the name
Default system sans (DejaVu) throughout; looks unstyled
Crop marks are printed for the empty third row, which has no badges
Print PDF is placed raster images with no live text (300 dpi effective, so sharp enough, but not vector)
The last two rows sit at the top of the 3-row grid, so they are not centred on the page

XVOL.craft_notes: Meets the spec and is legible, but looks like a default render: DejaVu Sans, cramped name leading, an oversized heavy bar label, and a pale grey rule with no use of the role colour beyond the bar. First-name size swings widely between badges. The PDF is rasterised and has stray crop marks on page 2.
XVOL.revision_notes: badge-11 added with an amber Speaker bar. Badges 05 and 09 now have a plum bar with white label (good contrast); per-pixel diff changes only the bar region. PDF page 2 now has Iris in slot 5. Nothing else drifted.

pairwise_round1.why: KCBV's left-aligned grid with role-coloured rule, tighter name block and tracked labels reads as a designed system; EMLW is clean but generic with loose, uneven name spacing.
EMLW uses a proper typeface with considered tracking and a vector PDF, where XVOL is default DejaVu with cramped leading and a heavy, crude bar label.
KCBV has a deliberate type scale, palette and print file; XVOL looks like an unstyled default render with tight leading and a rasterised PDF.
